```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# One-time installation (run these in the Console, NOT inside the Rmd):
# install.packages(c("haven", "DBI", "RMariaDB", "odbc", "jsonlite"))

library(haven)      # Stata, SAS, SPSS files
library(DBI)        # standard database interface
library(RMariaDB)   # MySQL / MariaDB driver
library(odbc)       # ODBC driver interface (Microsoft Access)
library(jsonlite)   # JSON from web APIs

# Folder containing the datasets (change here only if the location changes)
data_dir <- "C:/Users/USER/OneDrive/Desktop/Datasets imported in R"
```

# Introduction

In data science and analytics, data comes in different forms. Analysts must know how to bring data from different sources, such as statistical software, database management systems and web APIs, and how to work with built-in datasets in R.

This document demonstrates how R imports data from different environments.

Packages used:

- **haven**: reads files from other statistical packages (Stata, SAS, SPSS).
- **DBI, RMariaDB and odbc**: connect R to database management systems such as MySQL and Microsoft Access.
- **jsonlite**: brings in live data from the internet through web APIs.
- **Base R** (`read.csv`, `read.table`): reads structured text files.

# 1. Importing from Statistical Packages

## A. Stata data (.dta)

This dataset contains daily air quality measurements taken in New York City during May 1973.

```{r stata}
stata_data <- read_dta(file.path(data_dir, "session saved in stata.dta"))
names(stata_data)    # column names
head(stata_data)     # first 6 rows
dim(stata_data)      # rows and columns
```

## B. SAS data (.sas7bdat)

This dataset is a weekly panel for a skin and hair care product line, tracked across distribution centers.

```{r sas}
sas_data <- read_sas(file.path(data_dir, "DCSKINPRODUCT.sas7bdat"))
head(sas_data)
str(sas_data)        # data types and structure
```

## C. CSV files

This dataset contains information such as names and locations of customers of a business.

```{r csv}
csv_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "customers.csv"))
head(csv_data)       # first rows
names(csv_data)      # variable names
```

# 2. Importing from Database Management Systems (DBMS)

## A. MySQL

The database contains several tables, such as the employee table and the assignment table. If your MySQL user has a password, add it with `password = "your_password"` in `dbConnect()`.

```{r mysql}
con_mysql <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                       host = "localhost",
                       dbname = "wpdbase",
                       user = "root")

dbListTables(con_mysql)                          # all tables in the database
dbListFields(con_mysql, "employee")              # fields in the 'employee' table
employees <- dbReadTable(con_mysql, "employee")  # read the whole table
head(employees)
```

Querying specific rows with SQL: only the people working in the IT department.

```{r mysql-query}
IT_people <- dbGetQuery(con_mysql, "
    SELECT FirstName, LastName, Position
    FROM employee
    WHERE Department = 'IT'
")
IT_people
```

```{r mysql-close}
dbDisconnect(con_mysql)
```

## B. Microsoft Access (.accdb)

This database contains 6 students and their scores in class. The Access driver must match your R version (64-bit R needs the 64-bit Access driver).

```{r access}
con_access <- dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  .connection_string = paste0(
    "Driver={Microsoft Access Driver (*.mdb, *.accdb)};",
    "Dbq=C:/Users/USER/OneDrive/Documents/database to export to R.accdb;"
  )
)

students <- dbReadTable(con_access, "students")   # import the table
dbDisconnect(con_access)

head(students)
mean(students$Height)                             # mean height
```

# 3. Importing Data from Web APIs

The Cat Facts API returns interesting facts about cats (behaviour, night vision, hearing, etc.).

```{r api}
api_url   <- "https://catfact.ninja/facts"   # API endpoint
cat_data  <- fromJSON(api_url)               # fetch and parse JSON
facts_df  <- cat_data$data                   # extract the data frame
head(facts_df)
```

# 4. Using Built-in Datasets

R ships with datasets you can work with immediately. `iris` describes plants and their features.

```{r iris}
data("iris")
variable.names(iris)
```

Mean and standard deviation of petal length by species using `by()`:

```{r iris-by}
by(iris$Petal.Length, iris$Species, mean)   # mean petal length per species
by(iris$Petal.Length, iris$Species, sd)     # standard deviation per species
```
